title: Constitutional Reforms And Propaganda In Legislature
definition: The systematic campaign by early nationalists (Moderates) demanding expansion and reform of legislative councils (1905–1917), using the legislature as a platform for political education, exposure of colonial misrule, and economic critique.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Modern Indian History (GS-1), covering the Moderates' political methods, the evolution of constitutional reforms (Morley-Minto Reforms 1909), and the transformation of legislative chambers into sounding boards for Indian public opinion.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts of Moderate legislative politics and the demand for self-government.
Evaluate the provisions, limitations, and communal implications of the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms).
Apply high-yield mnemonics to retain legislative reforms and nationalist responses for Prelims and Mains.
prerequisites: Economic Critique of British Rule (Drain Theory)
